title: Work-Related Stress and Staff Wellbeing Policy
summary: How we prevent and manage work-related stress using the HSE Management Standards, and support the mental health and wellbeing of everyone who works for us, recognising the pressures of lone, time-bound home care work. It sets out our branch stress risk assessments, early action on signs of stress, individual stress risk assessments, support after distressing events and in a crisis, adjustments and returns to work, and how we check that the arrangements work. For all employees and the managers who plan and supervise their work.

keyPoints.intro: Your mental health matters to us as much as your physical safety. This is what to do if work, or anything else, is getting on top of you, and what we will do to help.
points: If stress, workload, your rota, travel or anything at work or at home is affecting you, tell your Field Care Supervisor, the HR Manager or any manager. You will never be criticised, disciplined or given fewer hours for asking for help.

Once we know stress is affecting you, the HR Manager or Registered Manager meets you within 5 working days to complete an individual stress risk assessment and agree changes, for example to your run, hours or duties.

If something at work leaves you too distressed to carry on safely, make the person safe and phone the office or the On-call Manager before you leave the home or drive on. We cover your visits and pay the rest of that day's rostered hours.
Never drive when you are too upset or exhausted to drive safely. Tell the office or the On-call Manager and we will pay for a taxi.

After a death, an emergency, an assault or anything you found distressing, your Field Care Supervisor contacts you within 1 working day and offers you a debrief within 3 working days. The debrief is your choice, and you never have to describe what happened.

The employee assistance programme gives you free, confidential counselling 24 hours a day. The number is on the branch office noticeboard and any manager will give it to you. The provider never tells us who uses it.

If a colleague says they are thinking of ending their life, take it seriously. If their life is at risk, call 999 and stay with them; otherwise help them contact their GP, NHS 111 or Samaritans. Tell a manager straight away.
Take your planned breaks and keep to the rest rules. Tell the Care Coordinator the same day if your visits cannot be done in the time allowed or your rota does not let you rest.
Take part in supervision, the September staff survey and the October staff discussion groups. What you tell us shapes our stress risk assessment and the changes we make.
What you tell us about your health stays confidential. The Care Coordinator and your supervisor are told only the changes agreed to your work, never the reason, unless you agree.

blocks.p: {{organisation}} treats work-related stress like any other risk to health at work: we assess it, reduce it at source and check that what we do works. The Health and Safety Executive defines stress as the adverse reaction people have to excessive pressures or other types of demand placed on them. Stress is not an illness, but it can make people ill and lead to mistakes in care and to staff leaving.

Our care workers work alone, travel between short, time-bound visits and are often the first to find a person who has fallen or died; Care Coordinators, Office staff and On-call Managers carry the rota and the calls that keep visits running. We plan work and support so that these pressures are manageable, and we support the mental health of everyone who works for us, whatever its cause, because staff who are well give safe, kind and reliable care.
{{organisation}} never treats anyone less favourably for saying they are struggling, asking for help, stopping work they cannot do safely or taking part in a stress risk assessment.

bullets: Assess and reduce the causes of work-related stress in each branch using the HSE Management Standards.
Act early on signs of stress through supervision, individual stress risk assessments and changes to work.
Support staff after distressing events, in a mental health crisis and when returning to work.
Give everyone confidential routes to help, and check through data and staff feedback that the arrangements work.

blocks.p: This policy applies to every employee of {{organisation}}, in every role and on every type of contract, including bank and variable hours, wherever they work: in people's homes, on the road, at the branch office or at home. Agency workers and students are supported by their agency or college; we include them in debriefs after distressing events at our visits and tell their agency or college the same working day so that it can offer its own support.

It covers work-related stress, which the law requires us to assess and control, and wider mental health and wellbeing, which we support whatever the cause, such as a bereavement, caring responsibilities, money worries or a long-term mental health condition. It does not cover the mental health of the people we support. Related arrangements are in these documents:

Management Standards
HSE's six areas of work design linked to stress when not managed well: demands, control, support, relationships, role and change.
Branch stress risk assessment
The written assessment of the risk of work-related stress in a branch against the six areas, with its action plan. It is one of the general risk assessments under the Health and Safety Policy.
Individual stress risk assessment
A confidential, structured conversation between an employee and the HR Manager or Registered Manager that identifies what is causing or adding to their stress and records the actions agreed.
Wellbeing plan
An optional note the employee writes with their supervisor: what keeps them well at work, their early signs of struggling and what helps. It is held in the restricted section of the staff record.
Distressing event

Any event a worker finds distressing, including the death of a person they support, finding a person collapsed, an emergency or resuscitation attempt, a safeguarding disclosure, violence or abuse, or a road collision.

blocks.p: The Directors approve this policy and fund the employee assistance programme, the occupational health provider, mental health first aid training, and the rota changes, second workers and adjustments that stress risk assessments require. They decline or renegotiate any package that cannot be delivered with realistic visit and travel times. The Nominated Individual receives the quarterly stress and wellbeing report, challenges any stress risk above the Directors' risk appetite, and reviews the Registered Manager's workload, hours and wellbeing at every supervision, as the Registered Manager Role and Absence Cover Policy sets out.

As Health and Safety Lead, the Registered Manager leads this policy in their branch: the branch stress risk assessment and action plan, stress impact checks before change, individual stress risk assessments when the HR Manager is unavailable or involved, adjustments the HR Manager cannot agree, and the quarterly stress and wellbeing report. The Deputy Manager covers these duties in their absence.

The HR Manager runs this policy day to day: receives every report that stress is affecting an employee, completes individual stress risk assessments, makes occupational health referrals, keeps the restricted section of the staff record, manages the employee assistance programme contract, runs the September staff survey and October discussion groups, sends the survey after a difficult event, and produces the monthly indicators.

subsections.heading: Field Care Supervisors and supervising Senior Care Workers

blocks.p: They cover wellbeing against the six Management Standards areas at every supervision, with a reminder of the employee assistance programme, and check that actions from any individual stress risk assessment are working. They watch for signs of stress at supervision, spot checks and every other contact and tell the HR Manager the same working day. The Field Care Supervisor gives the support after distressing events set out below.

Care Coordinators build rotas with realistic visit and travel time, breaks and rest, and build agreed adjustments into the rota before the worker's next shift. They are told the adjustment, never the reason. They take calls from distressed workers, cover their remaining visits and tell the Field Care Supervisor the same working day. On-call Managers do the same out of hours and hand over to the Care Coordinator by 10am the next working day.

The mental health first aider at each branch listens to colleagues in distress and directs them to the employee assistance programme, their GP or NHS 111. They do not diagnose or counsel. They tell the Registered Manager or Deputy Manager at once when someone may be at risk of harm, and are themselves offered a debrief with the Registered Manager within 3 working days of supporting a colleague in crisis.

Every employee takes their planned breaks and rest, raises concerns about workload or wellbeing early, takes part in surveys, discussion groups and stress risk assessments, treats colleagues with respect and tells a manager if they are worried about a colleague.

bullets: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, section 2, requires us to protect the health, safety and welfare of employees so far as is reasonably practicable. HSE states that employers have a legal duty to protect workers from stress at work by assessing the risk and acting on it.

The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, regulation 3, require a suitable and sufficient risk assessment, which includes the risk of work-related stress, reviewed when it may no longer be valid or after significant change. Because we employ five or more people, the law requires the significant findings to be written down.

Under the Equality Act 2010, a mental health condition is a disability when it has a substantial and long-term adverse effect on normal day-to-day activities; long-term means it has lasted, or is likely to last, at least 12 months (or the rest of the person's life). Where our arrangements put a disabled employee at a substantial disadvantage we must take reasonable steps to avoid it, and we may not ask the employee to pay for them.
Regulation 18 of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014 requires staff to receive appropriate support, supervision and appraisal to do their work.

blocks.p: The HSE Management Standards are HSE's recommended approach, not a legal requirement. Our policy is to use them as the standard for every stress risk assessment, at branch level and for individuals.

steps: Staff views: the anonymous September staff survey run by the HR Manager has two linked parts, and its work pressures check asks about each of the six areas. In October the HR Manager and a representative of employee safety hold at least two paid discussion groups in each branch using HSE's Stress Talking Toolkit: one between morning and evening runs for care staff and Field Care Supervisors, and one for Office staff, Care Coordinators and On-call Managers. Staff who cannot attend may join by video or send views to a representative.

Data: the Registered Manager reviews the previous 12 months of the indicators in Monitoring and review, with exit questionnaire themes, grievances and bullying reports, visit overruns, violence and abuse incidents and supervision themes.

Hazards and people: for each of the six areas the assessment records the hazards, the groups most at risk (for example new care workers, night and weekend workers, workers on long rural runs, sponsored workers living far from family, Care Coordinators and On-call Managers) and the controls in place.

Rating: each area is rated using the method in the Risk Assessment and Home Environment Risk Assessment Procedure. Any area with a residual score above 6, the Directors' risk appetite for staff health, safety and wellbeing, gets further actions. Any High or Very high residual risk also goes on the branch risk register under the Risk Management Policy.

Action plan: each action has a priority, an owner, the resources needed and a completion date, and goes into the service improvement plan. The plan is agreed at the Health and Safety Meeting with the representatives of employee safety and shared with all staff with the minutes within 10 working days.

Follow-through: actions are tracked in the service improvement plan and at each quarterly Health and Safety Meeting. An action that is not working is changed straight away, without waiting for the annual review.

bullets: Every year by 30 November, using the September survey and October discussion groups.

Within 7 days after a significant incident or change, as for every general risk assessment, including the death or serious assault of a colleague, or a capacity pause or business continuity activation once it has lasted 2 weeks.
Within 10 working days when a monitoring trigger in Monitoring and review is reached.

Before any planned change to the runs, hours, roles or base of 5 or more staff: the Registered Manager records a stress impact check in the assessment and consults the affected staff at least 10 working days before the change starts. Changes made in an emergency are checked within 7 days afterwards.

sections.heading: Home care pressures and our standing controls

blocks.p: These controls are in place in every branch. The branch stress risk assessment adds local actions.

rows: Demands

Too little travel time, visits too short for the care needed, split shifts, long days, early starts, night and on-call work and the fatigue they cause, late changes, emotionally demanding care such as end of life care, and difficult home environments.

Paid, realistic travel time, planned breaks, 11 hours' rest, a 60-hour weekly cap and the fatigue stop on full pay (Working Time, Rest Breaks and Travel Time Policy). Rota published by 12 noon each Thursday. Care that cannot be delivered in the visit time is reported to the Care Coordinator the same working day; the Care Coordinator reviews the visit length with the person within 7 days and asks the commissioner within 2 working days where it must agree more time (Care Plan Review Procedure). The Registered Manager pauses new packages when the rota cannot safely cover existing care.
Control
Little say over runs, changes at short notice and pressure to cover extra visits.

Recorded availability is respected. Extra visits outside contracted hours may be refused without any effect on hours offered later. Changes after publication are made on the CareFlow rota and the worker is phoned. Flexible working requests follow the Flexible Working and Family Leave Policy.
Support
Working alone with no colleague or manager on site, and long periods without seeing a colleague.

The office in office hours and the On-call Manager out of hours can always be reached by phone; On-call Managers answer at once or return a missed call within 15 minutes. A planned supervision or spot check about every 6 weeks, a paid staff team meeting at least every 3 months, the employee assistance programme, a mental health first aider in every branch and occupational health.
Relationships
Abuse from people we support, families or the public, and conflict or bullying between colleagues.

Every incident reported and acted on under the Violence and Aggression Towards Staff Policy; nobody is required to return to a home where they were harmed. Colleague complaints under the Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy; a request not to be paired with a colleague is met within 2 working days without loss of hours.
Role
Families asking for tasks outside the care plan, and uncertainty about what to do in an emergency.

The care plan and My care at a glance set out each visit. Staff never change the safe system of work at anyone's request and phone the office instead. No task is done without training and sign-off. Escalation routes are taught at induction.
Change
Packages starting, ending or suspended for hospital admission, new systems, and colleagues leaving.

Stress impact check and consultation before change. Policy change summaries and discussion at team meetings and supervision. Cancellation pay protects pay when a visit is cancelled less than 24 hours ahead.

blocks.p: Office and management roles carry their own pressures. Care Coordinators and Office staff may end abusive calls under the Violence and Aggression Towards Staff Policy; On-call Managers work within the on-call limits in the Working Time, Rest Breaks and Travel Time Policy and can always reach the escalation manager.

Lone workers are kept in touch: each month the HR Manager checks the supervision, training and rota records in CareFlow and lists any care worker who has had no supervision, spot check, team meeting, training or double-handed visit for 8 weeks, and their Field Care Supervisor phones them within 5 working days.

sections.heading: Recognising and acting on signs of stress

blocks.p: Signs in an individual include more absence or lateness, missed check-ins, more errors in daily visit notes or the eMAR, withdrawal, irritability, tearfulness, loss of confidence and changes in mood. Signs in a team include arguments, rising absence and turnover, and more complaints and grievances. A sign is a reason to ask, not to judge: the supervisor or manager who notices it speaks to the employee privately the same or next working day, asks how they are and listens, and suggests they see their GP if their health is affected.

steps: The HR Manager, or the Registered Manager where the HR Manager is unavailable or involved, meets the employee in private and in paid time at the branch office, by video or by phone, as the employee prefers, never in a person's home, a car or a public place. The employee may bring a colleague or trade union representative.

They go through the six areas as they apply to the employee: their run, hours, rest and tiredness, travel, the people they support, colleagues, role and recent changes, and anything outside work the employee chooses to share. They ask whether the employee has any thoughts of harming themselves and follow Distressing events and crises if so.

They agree actions, each with an owner and a date, such as a stable run near home, no split shifts or early starts for a time, longer gaps between visits, a break from a particular person's visits, more frequent supervision, an occupational health referral, the employee assistance programme or Access to Work mental health support.

Where the employee or the assessor thinks the employee cannot safely work as rostered, interim changes are made the same day. Contracted hours, or for variable-hours staff the hours already rostered, are paid in full.

The HR Manager records the assessment in the restricted section of the staff record and gives the employee a copy within 2 working days. The Care Coordinator and named supervisor are told only the changes to work, which are built into the rota before the employee's next shift.

The assessment is reviewed after 4 weeks, then at least every 3 months while any action is open, and within 5 working days whenever the employee asks or things get worse. It is closed when the employee and the assessor agree, and the closure is recorded.

Anything the HR Manager cannot agree is decided by the Registered Manager within 5 working days, with written reasons and the nearest alternative. An employee who disagrees may use the Grievance Policy and Procedure.

blocks.p: Every employee may also write a wellbeing plan with their supervisor at any time. It is voluntary, the employee decides what it says, and they may change or withdraw it whenever they wish.
If something at work, such as a distressing event, abuse or the pressure of the run, leaves you too distressed to carry on safely:

steps: Make the person safe and give any care that cannot wait, unless staying would put you at risk. If someone in the home is the cause, leave and act from a safe place under the Violence and Aggression Towards Staff Policy.

Phone the office, or the On-call Manager out of hours, and speak to a person before you leave the home or drive on, from outside if anyone there makes you feel unsafe. If nobody answers within 15 minutes, phone the Registered Manager or Deputy Manager directly.
Say whether the person is safe, what care is still due and whether the home and key safe are secure, and check out on CareFlow or give the time you left.

The office or On-call Manager agrees with you whether you can continue. If not, they arrange the care still due and cover your remaining visits under the Missed, Late and Short Visits Procedure; leaving early for this reason is never counted against you. The rest of that day's rostered hours are paid, and if you should not drive you go home by taxi at our cost.
A manager phones you before your next shift, and the Registered Manager (the Deputy Manager in their absence) agrees with you before that shift whether you are ready to work alone.

blocks.p: A worker who becomes physically ill during a run follows the same steps, but pay for the rest of the day follows the Sickness Absence Policy. After any distressing event at a visit, even when the care worker feels able to carry on, the office or On-call Manager checks that they are fit to go on before they travel to their next visit.

bullets: The Field Care Supervisor contacts the worker within 1 working day and offers a debrief within 3 working days, in paid time at the branch office, by video or by phone as the worker prefers. The debrief is also offered to colleagues who were involved or witnessed it. It is offered, never required, and the worker never has to describe the event: the facts go to the incident investigation under the Incident Reporting, Investigation and Learning Policy.

Within 4 weeks the Field Care Supervisor checks again with the worker, and in the same week the HR Manager sends the confidential survey after a difficult event. Only the HR Manager reads the survey answers, because they may include health details that supervisors do not see (Staff Personal Data and HR Records Policy).
The worker may ask not to visit that person or home for a time; the Care Coordinator makes the change from the next rota without loss of hours.
The employee assistance programme is offered every time. Signs of stress lead to an individual stress risk assessment.
After the death of a person we support, the core care team is told personally before their next shift and a group reflective session may be offered, as the End of Life Care Policy sets out.
Violence or abuse also follows the Violence and Aggression Towards Staff Policy, including the choice to stop for the rest of that day on full pay.

steps: Take it seriously, listen, and ask them directly whether they are thinking of ending their life.
If their life is at risk, they have seriously harmed themselves or they cannot keep themselves safe, call 999 and stay with them, or on the phone, until help arrives. Never leave them alone.
If they are not in immediate danger, help them contact their GP, NHS 111 using the mental health option, Samaritans or the employee assistance programme, and agree who they will be with.
Tell the Registered Manager or Deputy Manager at once (the On-call Manager out of hours). Do not promise to keep it secret when a life may be at risk.

The Registered Manager or Deputy Manager contacts the employee by the end of the next working day, and agrees with them before their next shift whether and how they work, including lone visits and driving, with occupational health advice where needed. Their visits are covered meanwhile, and any rostered hours we ask them not to work are paid. The manager records what was agreed in the restricted section of the staff record; the employee's health details never go in the incident log or daily visit notes. The person who first helped is offered a debrief within 3 working days.

blocks.p: The Registered Manager (the Deputy Manager in their absence) tells the team personally, by phone or in person, before they hear by other means where possible, and never by group message. A group debrief is offered within 3 working days, with the employee assistance programme and individual support. The branch stress risk assessment is reviewed within 7 days.

blocks.p: Counselling through the employee assistance programme agreed as an action in an individual stress risk assessment may be taken in working hours with the Care Coordinator's agreement and is paid, up to 6 sessions in any 12 months. Concerns about practices causing stress that are not resolved may be raised under the Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy.

sections.heading: Adjustments, absence and returning to work

blocks.p: We do not wait for a diagnosis, or decide whether someone is disabled, before making adjustments for stress or a mental health condition. Requests, interim arrangements, the workplace adjustment record and its reviews follow the Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy.

Stress-related absence is reported, paid and managed under the Sickness Absence Policy, including the named contact's call within 3 working days, the occupational health referral once the absence passes 7 days and phased returns. Nobody is asked to deal with work while off sick. Absence caused by work-related violence or aggression is recorded as a work-related injury and does not count towards review points.

Before the first shift after stress-related absence, the HR Manager or Registered Manager reviews the individual stress risk assessment with the employee, by phone or video if that is quicker, so that agreed changes are on the rota before they return. The return-to-work conversation and any phased return then follow the Sickness Absence Policy.

bullets: Health information goes only in the restricted section of the staff record (staff record documents, which CareFlow opens only to roles given the staff document permissions), as the Staff Personal Data and HR Records Policy sets out. CareFlow cannot hide one employee's documents from those roles, so the Registered Manager's and Deputy Manager's own health information is saved as a password-protected document that only the Nominated Individual can open, and the HR Manager gives a copy of a wellbeing plan to the supervisor who helped write it. It is shared further only with the employee's consent, or where someone's life or safety is at serious risk.

Where stress affects safe practice, for example medicines errors, missed check-ins or unsafe driving, the Registered Manager may set temporary changes to duties, such as no lone visits, medicines support or driving, on a written risk assessment reviewed at least every 4 weeks. This is never a sanction. Contracted hours, or for variable-hours staff the hours already rostered, are paid in full, and the Care Coordinator offers other suitable work in the same rota week.

Stress during a disciplinary, capability, attendance or safeguarding process does not stop it, but the process is adjusted, for example in timing, breaks or video meetings, unless occupational health advises that the employee is not fit to take part. A shortfall caused by ill health that no adjustment can overcome moves to the ill-health route in the Sickness Absence Policy.

Asking for help or using the employee assistance programme is never reported to the Home Office. The HR Manager explains to sponsored workers how any absence or change of hours affects their sponsorship, under the Right to Work and Sponsored Workers Policy.

blocks.p: The Registered Manager reviews the branch stress risk assessment within 10 working days, and tells the Nominated Individual, when stress-related absence days rise by 50% or more on the previous 3-month average, or when 3 or more individual stress risk assessments start in the same team or role in a branch in a quarter. The annual independent health and safety audit includes this policy.

The Registered Manager reviews this policy every 12 months, and sooner after a change in law or guidance, a serious incident, an inspection finding or when monitoring shows the arrangements are not working. The Directors approve it under the Policy Management and Document Control Policy, and every employee acknowledges it in CareFlow by the deadline in the Induction and Care Certificate Procedure and within 14 days of each new major version; a minor version does not need acknowledging again.
